modules.intro: Build the deck you present from. It is due before anyone presents, not on the day you present.
modules.title: Your deck
modules.aiNote: AI may make or edit images, suggest layouts, and tighten sentences you wrote. It may not generate the deck or write your process decisions for you.

blocks.content:
Eight slides. Slides 2 through 6 are one per station, in the order below. Put the station name on each of those slides.

```
                                            about
 1   TITLE       your name + trophy photo     15 sec
 2   BASE        H2D Laser                    30 sec
 3   COLUMN      Manual Mill                  30 sec
 4   PLATFORM    Axiom CNC Router             30 sec
 5   SHAFT       Manual Lathe                 30 sec
 6   TOPPER      xTool MetalFab               30 sec
 7   NUMBERS     nominal, measured, diff      60 sec
 8   FINDINGS    what it showed + ranking     60 sec
                                            -------
                                             4 min 45
```

On each station slide, two things: a photo of the part you made, and one process decision you made there. If a part broke, photograph what you have.

**A process decision is a choice you made that changed the part:** which tool, what speed or feed, how you held it, what order you cut in, or a setting you changed from the default. Being assigned to a machine is not a decision.

On slide 7, for every part: nominal, measured, and difference. **Difference is measured minus nominal. Keep the minus sign.**

How it has to look:

- 4:3 aspect ratio. Set it before you start.
- 25 words maximum on any slide except the title slide. Slide titles count. Numbers in a table do not count.
- Every slide has an image filling at least a third of the slide, except the title slide.

Build it in Google Slides, PowerPoint, or Canva. Turn view access on for anyone with the link, then open your link in a private window. **If it does not open there, it will not open for me, and the deck scores zero.**

AI is allowed for images, layout, and tightening sentences you wrote. Not for generating the deck. You will be asked about your own slides.

modules.intro: You walk the class through your trophy and what you found making it. Slides are on the screen. Your five parts are on the bench in front of you.
modules.title: Present your portfolio

blocks.content:
Seven minutes each. Five minutes presenting, two minutes of questions. At five minutes you stop, wherever you are.

How the days work:

- **Block 3:** presentations run across two class days, half the class each day. The order is posted before the first day.
- **Blocks 2 and 4:** every presentation happens in one class day.

Your deck is due before the first presentation day in every section. If you present on the second day, the deadline was still the first day.

What you cover in five minutes:

- The process decision you made at each of the five stations.
- Which process held its dimensions closest to nominal and which was furthest off. **Use the single largest difference on each part to decide.**
- Why. Name one of these four: the size of the tool or the beam, how the material behaves, how the part was held, or how the machine moves. Then tie it to one of your own numbers.

The two minutes of questions:

You will be asked **at least two questions**, from the instructor or the class. They are about what you did and what you measured, not about whether your choices were right. Everyone made the same five parts.

Reading a slide out loud is not an answer. If you do not know, say so and say what you would measure to find out.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: States a process decision at all five stations, each one a tool, setting, workholding, or sequence choice.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: States a qualifying decision at four stations, or at all five with one being a description of what was done rather than a choice.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: States a qualifying decision at two or three stations.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: States a qualifying decision at one station or none.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names the closest and furthest process using their own largest differences, gives a reason from the four listed, and ties that reason to one of their measured numbers.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Names both processes from their own numbers and gives a reason from the four listed, without tying it to a measured value.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Reads measurements aloud without naming which process was closest and furthest, or names them with no reason from the four.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Does not refer to their own measurements.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Answers both questions using something they did or measured that is not written on a slide.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Answers one question from their own work and answers the other by repeating slide content.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Answers both questions by repeating slide content, or answers one and cannot answer the other.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Answers neither question, or does not present.
